t: You're standing on Elizabeth Street, a road in Belgravia, in central London. The street takes its name from Elizabeth Leveson-Gower, a noblewoman who lived from 1797 to 1891. That's a long life, nearly ninety-four years, and her name is what remains of her here, written on the street signs. The material I have doesn't say more about her or about how the street came to carry her name, so I'll leave it there. Take in the Belgravia setting around you, and know that a woman's name is behind this one.
